newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour-will leave income tax rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour-will leave income tax rates unchanged.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party pledged on Thursday to leave income tax rates unchanged, keep inflation low and stick to the Conservative government's existing public spending plans for the next two years. Reiterating a 10 point contract, handwritten by Labour leader Tony Blair, the manifesto said, "There will be no increase in the basic or top rate of income tax.
"We will match the current targets for low and stable inflation of 2.5 percent or less."

As part of his promise to stick to existing spending plans for the next two years, the manifesto said a Labour government would enforce the so-called golden rule -- borrowing only to invest. The manifesto also said a Labour government would reform the Bank of England to ensure more effective, open decision making on monetary policy.

Labour's 10-point plan also put education as its number one priority as well as removing 250,000 young people from the dole queues, levying a one-off windfall tax on the "excess profits of the privatised utilities" to pay for the programme.
